easy.def: A long period of time in history.
examples: The dinosaur era was long ago.
This era is new.
We learned about an era.

more.def: A long period of history marked by something special.
examples: The dinosaur era ended millions of years ago.
The space era began when the first rockets flew.
We studied the era of the knights and castles.
I erase the mistake.
She erased the board.
He erased the word.

more.def: To remove writing or marks by rubbing them out.
examples: I erased my mistake with the eraser.
She erased the chalkboard.
He erased the word and wrote it again.

easy.def: A rubber you use to rub out pencil marks.
examples: I used an eraser.
The eraser is pink.
My pencil has an eraser.

more.def: A small piece of rubber or a cloth used to rub out writing or marks.
examples: The pencil's eraser was worn down to a nub.
She used an eraser to rub out the wrong answer.
The teacher cleaned the board with an eraser.
They erected a tent.
Workers erect a tall wall.
We erected a fort.

more.def: To build something, or to set it up straight.
examples: The campers erected their tents by the lake.
Workers erected a statue in the park.
The crew erected a tall fence around the field.
He stood erect.
The tree stands erect.
The flag is erect.

more.def: Straight and upright, not bent or leaning.
examples: The soldier stood erect with his shoulders back.
The tall pine stood erect in the wind.
She sat erect and listened carefully.

easy.def: Soil or rock being slowly washed or blown away.
examples: Erosion wears down hills.
Wind causes erosion.
Erosion made the canyon.

more.def: The slow wearing away of rock and soil by water, wind or ice.
examples: Erosion by the river carved a canyon.
Wind and rain cause erosion of the hills.
Trees help prevent erosion of the soil.
I erred on the test.
He erred in his math.
To err is human.
The students erred in adding the numbers.
It is better to err on the side of caution.
Anyone can err when they are in a hurry.

easy.def: A short trip to do a job.
examples: I run an errand.
Mom has errands.
I went on an errand to the store.

more.def: A short trip to do a small job, such as buying something.
examples: I ran an errand to the store for Mom.
Dad did errands on Saturday.
She went to the post office on an errand.

easy.def: Moving or acting in an unpredictable way.
examples: The ball took an erratic path.
An erratic path.
His moves were erratic.

more.def: Not following a regular pattern; hard to predict.
examples: The bat's flight was erratic.
The bus kept an erratic schedule.
The kite made erratic dives in the wind.
I made an error.
The error is small.
She fixed the error.

more.def: Something that is not right, a mistake.
examples: I made an error in my math.
The computer showed an error message.
She found and fixed the error in her story.
The volcano may erupt.
The room erupted in cheers.
Hot rock erupted from the top.

more.def: To burst out suddenly with force, as a volcano does, or as a noise does.
examples: The volcano began to erupt with smoke and hot rock.
The crowd erupted in cheers when the team scored.
The geyser erupts every hour in the park.

easy.def: A sudden burst, like a volcano.
examples: The eruption was loud.
We saw the eruption.
An eruption of lava.

more.def: A sudden burst of lava, steam or other force.
examples: The volcano's eruption sent ash into the sky.
An eruption of laughter filled the room.
The geyser's eruption shot water high.
